summary: IDS feed s064_single is degraded due to one-way traffic: 41 of 188 TCP sessions (21.8%) show only one direction, exceeding 10% threshold. IDS requires bidirectional visibility and will have reduced detection coverage. No other faults detected (no duplicates, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, VLAN or encryption issues).

findings.root_cause: Feed is delivering only a single direction of bidirectional conversations. Most likely the packet broker is fed from a single SPAN/mirror direction or only one leg of a TAP/bond, or asymmetric routing return path is not being mirrored/aggregated to this tool port. Name 's064_single' suggests single-sided capture.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true to track TCP state, reassemble streams, and correlate request/response for signature and anomaly detection. With 21.8% one-way sessions the IDS cannot see handshakes, will fail to reassemble, misses attacks that span both directions, and generates incomplete flow logs/false negatives.

params.source: mirror both RX and TX or both TAP legs to single tool port

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both directions into one coherent feed ensures the IDS sees client-to-server and server-to-client packets for the same session together, restoring stateful inspection and full detection coverage.
